answer: Inter-arrival cadence gating. Each identity operates a timing harbor: the system measures gaps between its signed actions and admits it only while those gaps stay within a learned band. Fresh identities must let a bridge period elapse—observed, low-volume traffic that holds the account dormant long enough to prove it is not a burst farm. Any sudden delta from the band freezes the identity until it re-earns admission, so an attacker pays real wall-clock time per identity, and parallel creation multiplies that cost linearly rather than letting one script fan out thousands at once.
